siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (4.5 in or 5 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

citations.citation: "Early Chicago Voter Lists" — the poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago (10 August 1833), the tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833, the election returns and poll list of 1834 filed 11 August 1834, and the 1835 poll list. Transcribed from the Illinois Regional Archives Depository originals by Ingrid Latimer Schulz, published in Chicago Genealogist XXV/4 (Summer 1993), and republished by the Genealogy Trails Transcription Team.

transcribes.work: Poll list for the first election of Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago (10 August 1833)
transcribes.note: 30 entries. Andreas says twenty-eight men voted at this election; the list prints thirty names. T-0542 searched for a count outside Andreas and found none — the Chicago Democrat did not exist until 26 November 1833 and its whole run to August 1835 carries no retrospective count of this poll — so the discrepancy STANDS, with the negative search recorded (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v004). On weight the thirty are the enrolments and Andreas's twenty-eight is an 1884 belief-statement ('It is believed') about the number of legal voters; neither count is repaired.

transcribes.work: Tax List of the Town of Chicago - 1833
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Names only — as published it carries no valuation, no lot and no figure, so it is not a ranked property roll (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v001).

transcribes.work: Election Returns - Poll List of 1834, filed 11 August 1834
transcribes.note: 115 entries. Andreas independently dates the second town election to 11 August 1834, which corroborates the list's own heading.

85 entries. THE LIST PRINTS NO DATE, AND IT IS NOT THE POLL BOOK OF THE THIRD TOWN ELECTION. That election is now dated from the town's own newspaper rather than from Andreas: the Chicago Democrat of 8 July 1835 announced the election of Trustees under the new charter for 'Friday of this week' and the issue of 15 July reported that it 'took place on Friday last' with the return — FRIDAY 10 JULY 1835, nine days after the 1835-07-01 scene date (claims/town_election_1835_democrat.json d001-d005). Andreas's town chapter, 'in July, 1835', is corroborated; his police chapter's 5 August 1835 is the day the newly elected board sat and passed the town's ordinance code over Hugunin's name as President. But that return gives single candidates 124 and 142 votes, which 85 men cannot cast, and six of the ten men who stood are absent from these 85 while the list runs unbroken from Adams to Wright — so this is a DIFFERENT poll, not a short printing of that one (claims/town_findings_voter_lists.json v003). Which poll is open; the county and state general election of Monday 3 August 1835 is the nearest candidate. Until it is settled, a name here evidences presence in Chicago in 1835 and not presence on any particular day.

what_it_supplies: 345 names of men who voted at, or were taxed by, the Town of Chicago in 1833, 1834 and 1835, as printed
which of the four lists each name stands on, and its position in that list
the courtesy and rank titles the lists print in front of a name (Col., Lt., Major, Dr.)

for the 1835 poll list: presence in Chicago during 1835, which is the strongest residence evidence this project holds short of a newspaper naming the man — but NOT presence on a stated day, because the list is undated and is shown not to be the poll book of the 10 July 1835 town election (T-0542)
what_it_does_not_supply: any address, street, lot or dwelling
any age, trade, household or family member
any date more precise than a list's own heading — and the 1835 list has no heading date at all
any woman, and any man who neither voted nor was taxed

citations.citation: Robert Fergus, Fergus' Directory of the City of Chicago, 1839 (Chicago: Fergus Printing Company, 1876) — Fergus' Historical Series No. 2; read from the Allen County Public Library Genealogy Center scan on the Internet Archive
what_it_supplies: A name, a trade and a street for 1,655 entries in the city of 1839 — the closest address list to 1835 this project can reach.
A trade for 976 of them at a stated street, which compiles into 102 street faces (Lake 199, Clark 94, North Water 83, South Water 72).

On printed page 37: six churches with their ministers, fifteen hotels, the public offices around the Public Square, the land office, the lighthouse, the theatre, two named building rows, the Dutch Settlement, and the fire that took the Tremont House on 27 October 1839.
what_it_does_not_supply: An 1835 residency. Four years late, and the ratified ladder never makes a resident from a later listing alone.

An address number that means anything, off Lake street. Fergus writes on printed page 3 that no street but Lake was numbered in 1839 and that 'the numbers now given are those of the present day' — 1876's. Only the street name crosses.
A count of its own entries. The volume states no number of names anywhere, so a reading of it cannot be closed against the book the way a census sheet closes against its printed totals.
